sources.title: JSON schema and validation
sources.text: Structured output asks the provider for JSON matching a declared schema. A JSON schema can specify property names and expected types. Always validate the returned object on the server, and separately check business rules such as whether an ID exists.

sources.title: Streaming and first token
sources.text: A streaming response sends small chunks as the model generates text. Time to first token measures how long the learner waits before seeing the first usable text, not how long the entire response takes. A stream should handle interruption and show incomplete output as such.

sources.title: Timeout, retry, and backoff
sources.text: Retry transient failures such as rate limits or temporary server errors with bounded exponential backoff and jitter. Avoid retrying invalid credentials or malformed requests. After streaming has shown text, do not silently replay the request.

results.referenceTruth: Citation presence is distinct from claim support; held-out cases reduce overfitting.

sources.title: Labelled evaluation cases
sources.text: Build a labelled evaluation set with a clear expected outcome for each case. Include realistic in-scope questions and off-topic questions. Keep development examples separate from an independent test set when estimating real generalization.

sources.title: Citation correctness
sources.text: Citation correctness asks whether the cited section actually supports the response. An existing citation ID is only a structural check. Human reviewers can also check claim support, which requires reading the section and the answer together.

sources.title: Latency percentiles
sources.text: A median describes a typical run, while the 95th percentile highlights slow requests. Label the environment and warm-up conditions when reporting latency. Keep diagnostic outcomes and failures rather than reporting only successful runs.
